subject: Renewal structure: architected ramp & retention incentive
messages:
From: Sara Levin <sara.levin@novamed.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@novamed.com>, Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Upcoming renewal and expansion — term options & ramping

Hi Rachel,

Our contract is up 12/31 and usage has outpaced our current commit. We expect another 55% increase in Q1 usage as we onboard two product lines. We want to align the renewal structure to our fiscal plan across 2027 — ideally something that smooths burn while giving us flexibility to scale.

Key asks:
- Options for a multi-year term vs 1-yr with staged top-ups (we are open to 2–3 year)
- A ramp schedule (phased commit increases tied to milestones) so we don't overcommit up front
- Clarity on auto-renew clauses and an opt-out window for procurement
- Retention incentive / onboarding credits to offset our initial Q1 spike

Can you put together 2–3 concrete proposals (pricing impact and operational timing) and a short mutual action plan so procurement/legal can review? If possible, loop in commercial finance and any approval owners for credits.

Attaching current usage report and our forecast.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Levin
Head of Platform Partnerships
Novamed Health

Attachments: Novamed_usage_Q3_2026.csv (attachment)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Levin <sara.levin@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal and expansion — term options & ramping

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and context. Appreciate the forecast; this is exactly the kind of renewal we'd like to structure to avoid short-term overcommit while supporting your growth. I pulled together three options below and attached a one-page MAP and a PDF with pricing impact. High level: we can (A) keep a 12-month cadence with staged top-ups, (B) do a 24-month staged ramp with mid-term true-up and onboarding credits, or (C) sign a 36-month fixed commitment for a deeper, front-loaded discount.

Options (high level):
1) Option A — 12-month, flexible top-up
   - Baseline commit: current annualized run-rate (no discount)
   - Staged top-ups: two scheduled top-ups (1/1 and 4/1) allowing you to add capacity at pre-agreed pricing
   - Auto-renew: standard auto-renew with 60-day opt-out window
   - Credits: no retention credit; onboarding credits available as professional services billable credits

2) Option B — 24-month architected ramp (recommended)
   - Year 1: 70% of forecasted 2027 usage committed, Year 2: 100% of forecast
   - Mid-term true-up: prompted by >20% variance vs forecast; limited to one true-up
   - Discount: 10% year-over-year blended; retention incentive: $50k in token credits applied in Q1 to offset spike
   - Auto-renew: opt-out at renewal anniversary with 90-day notice; procurement-friendly termination right for material regulatory changes

3) Option C — 36-month fixed commit (price stability)
   - Fixed commit equals forecast with 15% discount, but limited rollover for underutilization (use-it-or-lose-it with limited carryover)
   - Retention incentive: larger professional services credit in lieu of token credits

Next steps I recommend:
- Internal approval for the $50k token credit for Option B (deal_id RDW-9381)
- Legal to take a look at the opt-out language for auto-renew
- We prepare a short MAP + SOW to align milestones for ramp triggers and onboarding acceptance criteria

I attached: MAP_20261112_Novamed.xlsx (mutual action plan) and redwood_renewal_options.pdf (pricing matrix). If this looks good, I can set up a call with Karthik and Rishi to walk procurement through the options.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: MAP_20261112_Novamed.xlsx (attachment); redwood_renewal_options.pdf (attachment)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Novamed RDW-9381 — credit approval question

Rachel / Rishi —

Thanks for drafting the options. I like Option B as a balance of protection + growth. A couple items for approval:
- The $50k token credit request is outside standard playbook for a 24mo (we usually authorize up to $25k). If we want to move to $50k, I need Marissa's sign-off.
- Finance wants the credits expressed as token units and not as a straight cash equivalent; that keeps billing and revenue recognition straightforward. Can we translate $50k into token units in the MAP (e.g., 3.2M tokens applied over Q1)?
- Legal will want clearer language on the single true-up and the 90-day opt-out; Rishi will take that offline with legal.

If Marissa approves, recommend we lead with Option B in the external meeting and present Option A as a fallback. Karthik

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 09:30 Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick note — procurement asked specifically about auto-renew opt-out timing.
> I flagged 90-day to be conservative but open to 60-day if that helps sign.
> 
> —Rachel
